about: Maggie's eye, from her test set, her edits and the calibration review she approved on Nov 15. Saved to taste_profiles by scripts/save-taste.ts.

rules.rule: Extra details the original doesn't have (a slit, a pleated bust, ruching, a cut-out) are counted once, as an extra. They lower other parts only when they change the outline.
rules.source: test set, edited by Maggie, reworded by calibration review

rules.rule: The fabric's look carries the piece: prefer fabrics that hang, drape or lie flat the way the original's does. Avoid thin or costume-shiny fabrics.
Keep the original's proportions, length and the scale of its details: short and cinched stays short and cinched, floor-length stays floor-length, big trim stays big, a slim heel stays slim.
rules.source: test set, reworded by calibration review

rules.rule: A matching word in a title (velvet, bodysuit, leather) earns nothing by itself. Judge material by how the surface looks and hidden construction by how the piece looks worn.
rules.source: test set, reworded by calibration review

rules.rule: The original brand's own pieces (the same piece in another color or another style from the label), the original's own photos and used or resale listings aren't dupes.
rules.source: test set, reworded by calibration review

rules.rule: Embellishment should be fairly literal: beading should read as beading and pearls as pearls. Sequins standing in for beading often, but not always, look cheaper.
For shoes, the toe shape, heel and overall profile should look close to one-for-one. Less literal options are still welcome when the profile matches, such as pebbled instead of smooth leather.

Looks come first. Similar fabric quality is a plus, not a requirement: lining, tailoring or a specific fiber (cashmere, wool, silk) only decides a match when the shopper switches Fabric must match on.
